corrections.claimed_speedup: Paper (FAST '24), per search snippet only: 2.27x higher throughput than FUSE in random read benchmarks, parity with Ext4 in sequential I/O. The 6.46x user-space time figure was not seen in any opened source.
corrections.caveats: Numbers come from a search-result snippet of the FAST '24 paper (usenix.org/system/files/fast24-cho.pdf is egress-blocked); the repo README has no numbers. Needs a patched Linux 5.15.0 kernel and kernel driver; RFUSE_NUM_IQUEUE must be set to the machine's core count before building. Baseline is stock FUSE, not a listed baseline. Retier candidate to B once the paper is reachable.

notes: GPL-2.0 LICENSE, 76 stars, 17 forks, last commit 2025-05-08 (active), confirmed on github.com. Paper PDF at https://www.usenix.org/system/files/fast24-cho.pdf is blocked here; a retier check from an environment with usenix.org access could raise it to B.

tier_reason: The README quick benchmark compares rg with git grep, ag and GNU grep on the Linux kernel tree on an Intel i9-12900K, but gives no compiler or flags and is first-party, so C. The mmap-versus-buffer numbers are from the blog, which was not opened.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README (Linux kernel tree, '[A-Z]+_SUSPEND' word search): rg 0.082s vs git grep -P 0.273s (3.34x), ag 0.443s (5.43x), GNU grep via git grep -E with UTF-8 locale 2.670s (32.70x). Blog snippet only (not verified): linux_literal 0.334s without mmap vs 1.611s with mmap; subtitles_literal 0.268s with mmap vs 0.336s without.
corrections.caveats: Search-engine speed dominates, not file I/O alone; it is a CLI tool, not a library (reuse is through the grep-* / ignore crates). The README benchmark is a single first-party run with no compiler or flags stated. mmap numbers come from a burntsushi.net blog snippet only. MIT OR Unlicense is OSI-approved; the Unlicense option is a public-domain-style dedication with no patent grant.
